CEICA v1.0.0: Cost-effectiveness and incremental cost analysis.

Cost-effectiveness and best buys follow the rules of IWR Planning Suite II, the certified USACE tool, including ties, duplicates and the No Action base. The Utoy Creek example reproduces the published analysis.

CEICA is not a certified planning model. Keep the Excel calculator with the decision record; its IWR input sheet supports an independent re-run in IWR Planning Suite II.

Source and issues

The four stages

  1. Inputs. Study settings, sites and alternatives, benefits at target years and costs. Under Study, How benefits are measured lists the modules that add up to each alternative's benefit (for example, riparian and instream); their values are entered under Benefits. Everything recomputes as you type.
  2. Sites. A plan is cost-effective when no other gives the same output for less, or more output for no more. Best buys have the lowest incremental cost per unit. Confirm the alternative each site carries forward.
  3. Watershed. Every combination of the carried actions. Choose the final array (the best buys by default), say whether each step is worth it, and pick the tentatively selected plan.
  4. Report. Download each figure (PNG, SVG) or table (Excel, CSV), the figures-and-tables document (Word, PDF) or everything in one .zip, with the Excel calculator. Document settings holds the document's title, Prepared by and date. The document stays a draft until every readiness item is checked.

Keys

Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo (outside text fields). Hover a plan to highlight it in the charts and tables; click a mark to pin the highlight; Esc clears it.

Saving your work

Your work is saved in this browser as you go, on this computer only. Clearing the browser's site data deletes it, so use Save to download the project file, the durable copy. CEICA runs entirely in this browser, so nothing you enter is sent anywhere.

v0.1.0 (2026-09-27)

  • CE/ICA that follows IWR Planning Suite II, ties and duplicates included.
  • Average annual outputs and costs, with interest during construction and OMRRR.
  • Watershed plans from every combination of site actions, rules included.
  • Decisions: recommendations, final array and TSP, flagged when results change.
  • Benefit modules: habitat units, index x quantity, average values or STAF.
  • STAF: function scores roll up to the ECI; import SFARI, EASI or DEEP exports.
  • Inputs: paste from Excel, with undo, redo and autosave in the browser.
  • Report: every figure and table, a Word or PDF document, or all in one .zip.
  • Excel calculator with live formulas; edit it and import it back.
  • Examples: Utoy Creek as published, and a STAF demonstration.
